newsitem.title: USA: Gecamines said to be unaffected by rebel activity.
newsitem.headline: Gecamines said to be unaffected by rebel activity.

text.p: Rebel activity in Zaire is not yet affecting operations at Gecamines, the state-owned copper and cobalt producer, which is also recovering from a strike earlier this year, a source close to the company said.

Gecamines produced 40,000 tonnes of copper and 5,000 tonnes of cobalt in 1996,the source said, adding it was difficult to forecast output this year because of an earlier strike, and whether rebels would stop output if they captured the plant in the country's southern area of Shaba.
"We were a little bit affected by the strike we had and we should be at a little bit less than the level we were looking at," the source said.
But supply lines to the plant and routes for shipments were still operating.
Gecamines' copper production is insignificant by world standards though cobalt output is relatively more substantial.
"But I think there is enough cobalt around and this situation did not come out of the blue. I think it has been discounted by the market," the source said.
Minor metals officials from across the world were here to attend a Metal Bulletin seminar.

Gecamines sells mainly lower grade cobalt, 99.3 to 99.4 percent metal. Only spot deals are done in the U.S. but the company does have some long-term commitments to customers in Japan and Europe but there does not seem to be any major concerns among those clients in light of the rebel activity, the source said.
"I don't see any price spikes. I am getting the feeling that cobalt is entering a period of prolonged stability," he added.
Even if rebels captured the mines and production plant, output would only be stopped temporarily at most because it was an important hard currency earner, the source said.
